items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The only thing I knew about Warmack was that he was from Louisville, Ky.

ctx.x: But I never complained because I was working with the best jazz musicians as a group that I had ever worked with. The Scott Brothers, Don Frye and Dickie Wells had New York experience and I was learning more and more about music and improving my style which was different from Frank Newton. It was a good thing to have two trumpet players in the same orchestra with different styles who worked well together in the ensemble.

We were like brothers that loved each other and the band was sounding better and better/with each rehearsal when the next offer came for a one week engagement. We never realized the actual quality of our playing until we were engaged to replace an orchestra called Warmack at the Arcadia Ballroom in Buffalo, New York and alternated with the house band who were known as the Buffalodians. The only thing I knew about Warmack was that he was from Louisville, Ky.

But the "Buffalodians" was an orchestra well known in the eastern states and were in the same category as the CASALOMA orchestra which was one of the best white orchestras ever organized. It was the first time that we had played in a dance hall that engaged two orchestras at the same time.
